references.text: The Lord cursed the ground because of Adam's sin, which provides direct context for why Lamech prophesied that Noah would comfort them from the toil and pain caused by the cursed ground.
Cain is cursed from the ground, reinforcing the theme of the curse over human labor with the earth.
Noah finds favor in the Lord's eyes, confirming Lamech's prophecy that Noah would have a special role in God's plan.
Noah begins to cultivate the ground after the flood, which can be seen as a partial fulfillment of the prophecy that he would bring comfort from the toil with the earth.
Hebrews 11:7 mentions Noah's faith when he built the ark, showing his role in saving humanity – a continuation of the theme of comfort and salvation.
